text:
The judge should instruct the jury on self-defense, because the father’s belief that he was in imminent danger of death or serious bodily harm was reasonable under the circumstances as he perceived them, even if the son was not actually under the influence of drugs and did not intend to harm him. The instruction should explain that self-defense applies if the defendant honestly and reasonably believed force was necessary to prevent imminent harm, and that the jury must assess reasonableness from the defendant’s perspective at the time.  
CONFIDENCE: 90
